A compliance policy judges a device: it defines rules such as minimum OS version, encryption, password strength or location, then marks each device compliant or noncompliant, and that verdict can gate access through Conditional Access. A configuration profile changes a device: it pushes settings like Wi-Fi, VPN, certificates or restrictions. One evaluates, the other configures, and most tenants use both together.

A compliance policy lives in Intune and decides whether a device meets your standards. A Conditional Access policy lives in Entra and decides whether an access attempt is allowed. Compliance produces the verdict; Conditional Access acts on it. Compliance evaluates the device and reports the state; Conditional Access evaluates the state and grants access or blocks it. Compliance is a one-time evaluation of your fleet. Conditional Access is an evaluation that happens on every access attempt. Compliance changes the device state. Conditional Access changes the tenant state. Compliance works even when the app is not enrolled. Conditional Access works only on enrolled apps.
